<document name="How Fernwood runs.docx" pages="4">
[Page 2]
Hiring and onboarding
Hiring managers open roles and run their own candidates: Priya for engineering and design roles, Dev for sales. A candidate moves from applied to a phone screen, interviews, an offer, and then hired, or is rejected at any point. Anyone at Fernwood can see the open roles and refer someone.
Interviewers write a scorecard after every interview. Offers above the salary band for the role need Wade's approval before they go out.
When someone is hired, Aisha Khan plans their first week: a plan with tasks for IT (Jon Bell sets up the laptop and accounts), the manager and a buddy. A new starter gets their software seats (Slack, Google Workspace, 1Password and the tools their team uses) in our tools list, which Jon keeps.

</document>

<document name="Fernwood policies.pdf" pages="38">
[Page 7]
Onboarding policy
When a candidate is hired, a first-week plan starts for them with their name, start date and
manager. Aisha Khan picks a buddy.
The plan has tasks for IT, the manager and the buddy. Jon Bell gets the IT task: laptop,
accounts and the new starter's software seats.
When the plan moves to the first week, the new starter's seats are added to the tools list.

</document>

Latest message from Wade Wilson:
Set up Onboarding: A first-week plan for each new starter. When someone is hired, a first-week plan starts with their name, start date and manager. Aisha picks a buddy. The plan has tasks for IT, the manager and the buddy. Jon gets the IT task: laptop, accounts and software seats.

Its rules, from the policies:
- When a plan starts, Aisha is asked to pick a buddy for the new starter.
- When a plan starts, tasks are created for IT, the manager and the buddy, and Jon gets the IT task.
- When the plan moves to the first week, the new starter's software seats are added to the tools list.

Where it connects to what is already built:
- Hired starts a first-week plan in Onboarding
- a new starter gets seats in Tools and budgets
